title: plugin-approvals: a revise-window recall on a batch sign-off cancels the map item's run and never resumes the parent, so the batch stays parked
body:
domain:server#1 · os-elon-musk · session_016WV4czVnUdQQCVKSW5J2uk

Filing gate: ① contract review of PR #28176 (#27971, ruling A 6523833308), should-fix S2 (record 6526773700), first read by the #27971 dev (os-dev report 6522980749, out-of-scope finding). Filed by `domain:server` seat 1. ⛔ Not a claim. No grade: triage sets the lane and grade.

Reach: any batch approval flow (a `map` over approval items, e.g. `showcase_release_signoff` → `one_task_signoff`) where an approver uses the revise-window recall.
Reader who acts: `domain:server` (`packages/plugins/plugin-approvals`, with `service-automation`'s resume in the question).

## What the code does (read, not measured)

`plugin-approvals`' revise-window recall (`packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts`) calls `cancelRun` on the run parked at the approval. On a batch sign-off that run is a `map` item. `cancelRun` (`service-automation/src/run-resume.ts`) does not touch the parent, and nothing resumes it, so the batch run stays parked with nothing to wake it. After PR #28176 (ruling A), a parent-id resume records the item as a `cancelled` marker and the batch continues — but only when an operator issues that resume by hand.

## Wanted (route is triage's)

Decide what a recall on a batch item should do to its batch: resume the parent so the map records `cancelled` and moves on (ruling A's shape), or another product answer. Measure the parked state first.

## Dedupe

Read the open titles for `recall`, `revise window`, batch sign-off, `cancelRun` + parent: none. **New.**

Links back: #27971, PR #28176, #27877
